text:
maria: Heads up — trying to nail behaviour when someone arrives via a deep link into a nested sidebar group. Should we preserve scroll & expanded groups or always collapse and focus?
ashok: I vote preserve. Users coming from email links expect context. :eyes: Too jarring to drop them at top.
lev: Preserve is nicer UX but implementation choices matter — store in URL vs localStorage. URL makes it shareable, localStorage makes it simpler.
olivia: Maybe hybrid: use hash fragment for immediate anchor (e.g., #section=integrations) and localStorage for ephemeral UI state like expanded groups. If someone explicitly shares, use `?nav=` query.
sam: Caution: localStorage persists across devices and sessions. We should key by workspace id and have TTL or clear on workspace switch.
maria: Agreed on workspace-keying. Proposal: `navScroll:{workspaceId}` and `navExpanded:{workspaceId}`. Clear on explicit sign-out or 30d.
ryan: Accessibility note — if we restore scroll, we must also move focus to the landing heading and add `aria-current="true"` so screen readers don't get lost. Announce via aria-live if appropriate.
design-bot: Proposed minimal URL contract for PR: `/workspaces/:wsId/apps/:appId?nav=group-3&anchor=routes#breadcrumbs` - `nav` optional shallow state (sharable) - `anchor` jump target for in-page focus - `#breadcrumbs` used by back-button/fragment behavior
ashok: Also use `history.replaceState` when auto-restoring so we don't bloat the back stack. Users expect Back to go to previous app, not many replace events.
olivia: Edge case: if the anchored item was removed or renamed, fallback to parent group and surface a small toast like "Target not found, showing closest match". This avoids 404-like feel.
sam: Implementation note for eng: React Router v6 lazy routes mean DOM may not exist at initial mount. Restore scroll after `dataLoaded`. Example: `await waitFor(() => mounted && dataLoaded)` before `scrollTo`.
maria: Quick copy nits: change breadcrumb label from "Routes" to "HTTP routes" in shared contexts to avoid ambiguity. And change the expand affordance text to "Show sections" for better screen-reader clarity.
lev: Tiny perf concern: storing full arrays of expanded node ids per workspace could grow; store an LRU of last N groups or a compressed bitset? But realistically it's tiny. Maybe limit to last 20 expanded nodes.
ryan: Could run an experiment: 50% preserve expanded state + scroll, 50% collapse + focus. Measure task success for deep-links and time-to-action.
maria: I'll sketch the PR with the URL contract, localStorage keying, and the accessibility focus changes. Will include the `history.replaceState` pattern and TTL plan.
olivia: I'll review copy once you have the branch. Ping me for microcopy and aria labels. :sparkles:
sam: FYI devops: if we're using localStorage heavily, ensure no PII gets stored. Only store UI ids.
design-bot: Implementation snippet to include in PR notes: `js const key = `navScroll:${wsId}`; const pos = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key) || 'null'); if (pos) window.scrollTo(0, pos.y); // restore focus setTimeout(() => container?.focus(), 0);`
maria: Thanks all — I'll draft and tag people. If anyone has strong objections to the hybrid approach (hash + localStorage + optional `nav` query) speak now or in the PR. :+1:
